answer.policy_title: Evolent Clinical Guideline 1770 for Shoulder Arthroscopy (previously National Imaging Associates, Inc. Clinical Guidelines: Shoulder Arthroscopy)
answer.effective_date: Last Revised Date: November 2024 / Implementation Date: July 2025
criteria_quotes:
Non-operative management, when required, will be specified within the clinical indications below and may include one or more of the following:
● Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program
● Rest or activity modification
● Application of heat or ice
● Minimum of 4 weeks of oral NSAIDs (if not medically contraindicated)
● Single injection of corticosteroid and local anesthetic into subacromial, intra-articular space, or bicipital groove

Surgical repair of a partially torn rotator cuff or excision of an area of calcific tendinopathy may be necessary when all the following criteria are met:
[...] Unless worsening symptoms develop, Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least 6 weeks of physical therapy or a properly instructed home exercise program

Surgical repair of a small full-thickness rotator cuff tear (< 1 cm) may be necessary when all the following criteria are met:
[...] Unless worsening symptoms develop, failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment*, including physical therapy or a properly instructed home exercise program

*NOTE: The requirement for conservative, non-operative treatment is waived in individuals < age 55 with an acute traumatic tear (onset of shoulder pain attributed to a specific traumatic event with no prior history of significant shoulder pain). For ages > 55, non-operative treatment may be waived on a case-by-case basis.

Surgical repair of a medium or large full-thickness rotator cuff tear may be necessary when the following criteria are met:
● Significant progression of a full-thickness tear on serial imaging performed at least 12 weeks apart (at least 50% increase in tear size) OR
● When ALL of the following criteria are met:
  o Reproducible rotator cuff pain patterns (lateral arm, deltoid pain not radiating past the elbow, night pain, or pain with overhead motions)
  o Functional loss (age-appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs), occupational, or athletic)
  o Positive impingement signs and/or tests on exam (Hawkins, Neer, Jobe test or reproducible pain when arm is positioned overhead with relief of pain when arm is repositioned below the plane of the shoulder)
  o MRI or ultrasound demonstrates a medium or large full-thickness tear (1-5 cm)

answer.notes: Tufts Health Plan delegates its Joint Surgery (Musculoskeletal) Program prior authorizations to Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates / NIA). The applicable clinical policy for CPT 29827 (shoulder rotator cuff repair) is Evolent Clinical Guideline 1770 (previously NIA_CG_318). Under this guideline, conservative care duration requirements vary significantly by tear severity: 12 weeks of non-operative care (with 6 weeks of physical therapy) is required for partial-thickness tears; 6 weeks of non-operative care is required for small (<1 cm) full-thickness tears; and conservative trials are waived entirely for acute traumatic tears in individuals under age 55 (and reviewed case-by-case for individuals over age 55).
